correctness.rationale: For tree T and selected edge subset S, contracting all T\S edges produces a tree Q_S with |S| edges, and any geodesic in T contains exactly the Q_S-distance many selected edges. Therefore S edge-GP iff diam Q_S<=2. When |S|>=2, Q_S must be a star with unique center, a connected vertex component K of T\S and S=delta_T(K). Conversely each nonempty connected K with |delta K|>=2 gives a unique valid S. For S empty there is one K=V(T); for |S|=1 both sides of deleted edge are possible centers, hence subtract |E(T)|z. A rooted highest-selected-vertex recurrence gives B_v=product_child(z+B_child) and C_T=B_root+z sum_{v≠root} B_v. Forest EGF factors componentwise. Every complement component has an original leaf; maximum boundary equals number of leaves iff K contains every branching vertex, and each terminal arm admits one independently chosen boundary cut, proving product arm length. Path and isolated-node boundaries are separately handled. Independent geodesic and connected-boundary enumeration on a seven-vertex tree returned identical [1,6,15,10,2] counts and the leading coefficient 2.
residual_risks: Connected-boundary identity is specific to trees; graph cycles obstruct quotient-star bijection.
Two-edge coefficient for paths is binomial of edge count, and isolated vertex is constant 1.

value.rationale: The full coefficient distribution of edge-general-position sets is a natural combinatorial refinement of the established leaf-count maximum. The new arbitrary-tree connected-boundary bijection yields an exact dynamic program and the number of maximum sets even when a tree has several branching vertices. This precise count is not determined by earlier scalar or spider-special-case results and is plausibly useful for graph parameter enumeration.
residual_risks: The boundary recursion alone is standard tree dynamic-programming algebra; mathematical value rests on the global edge-general-position bijection and complete coefficients.

scientific_limitations: No claim about graph cycles, root-realness, unimodality or arbitrary graph families.
